precepts.text: Ye shall seek me and shall not find me: when your fear cometh as desolation, then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
“Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, thither ye cannot come.” The Old Testament already spoke it: “When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you. Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me.”

They will not. The same words Christ spoke to the Pharisees and chief priests are written in Proverbs, against those who would not hear. When Christ, the apostles and the prophets spoke in the New Testament, their conversation was reiterating what the Old Testament was saying, and they could substantiate it with the text.

precepts.text: Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer: here is the worldly sorrow. When the affliction increases, after being wicked the whole time, now you are calling on the Lord, and the line is no longer available. For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord: they would none of my counsel; they despised all my reproof. Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way: if you are out there sowing sin, that is what you are going to reap.
precepts.point: For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: to our inheritance. But the sorrow of the world worketh death: that is the sorrow of the man of the field, the bitter cry over what he himself threw away. We have to be sincere when we come to the Lord and have that godly sorrow; we cannot be faking it.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Paul says “the sorrow of the world worketh death.” Here is what that worldly sorrow looks like: “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me”. When the Lord increases the affliction, after you have been wicked the whole time, now you are calling on the Lord: it's getting real down here, the persecution is on, I ain't got no food. You call, and the line says the number you have dialed is no longer available to you, dummy. You'll seek him early, like getting on a pre-call, and you still won't find him. You won't have any connection to the Lord on that day.

Why? “For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. They had the carnal mind, the mind of Cain and Esau, and cast the word behind their back like their father did. “They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.” They literally threw the word behind their back, and a lot of our brothers and sisters do that. We all have to examine ourselves.

“Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.” If you are out there sowing sin, that is what you are going to reap.

That is Esau's sorrow. He sold his birthright, then realized, damn, I want that blessing back, and cried bitterly over what he himself threw away. So we have to be sincere when we come to the Lord and have the real godly sorrow that works repentance to salvation, to our inheritance, not to be repented of. We can't be out here faking the funk.

precepts.text: Turn you at my reproof, and I will pour out my spirit unto you: the laws come before the spirit.
precepts.point: I will render double unto thee: for your shame ye shall have double, everlasting joy, and your seed known among the Gentiles, so that all who see your children acknowledge them as the seed the Lord has blessed. Write the chain of events: awakening, tribulation, World War III, Armageddon where Christ makes his advent, deliverance, wilderness, kings and priests.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
Zechariah says turn you to the stronghold; Proverbs says “Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.” God's reproof is his laws.

So there is a stipulation to get God's Holy Spirit: you must turn at God's reproof. The laws come before the spirit. Only when you turn to his laws will he pour out his spirit on you and make known his words to you.

That is why all these dumb Christians that say they have the Holy Spirit and won't keep a commandment do not have it. They have Satan on them. Turning to the stronghold, for us prisoners of hope, means turning at his reproof and keeping his laws.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction. None of them has a Bible in front of him; it is all off the top of the dome, pride and lasciviousness, the carnal side. Isaiah 34:16 says seek ye out of the book of the Lord and read. The world sees him say he is an Israelite and equates it to all of us; that is Satan's chess move to add affliction to our bonds, so we will correct all folly, Christian or Israelite, without partiality.
precepts.point: Believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God, because many false prophets are gone out into the world. You try them with the Bible. That goes for the Christian church too, and for anyone who says he believes on Christ and calls himself an Israelite.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
One thing shows up with this one, the last one, and all these so-called leaders: they don't even use the Bible. Every time you see them teach, it is pride, and when they do try to use the Bible, they make something up. You never see them following according to the scripture.

“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge”. You show your fear of the Lord, and that you have knowledge, by sitting down and reading, as Isaiah says, “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”. But these men have no Bibles in front of them. Everything is made up off the top of the dome, full of pride and lasciviousness. There is no fear of the Lord there.

And “fools despise wisdom and instruction.” They won't follow wisdom, won't follow basic instructions, won't look in the book. Everything is of the flesh, their sensual, carnal side. He goes on podcast interviews and freestyles the whole thing, and nothing biblical comes out.

But people see him say he's an Israelite and equate that to all Israelites. See the chess move: Satan puts these things in place because somebody is going to add affliction to our bonds. So we are not going to sit back. We will say something, and that goes for the so-called Christians and for brothers in this truth, Israelites alike. We will correct all folly, and we won't be partial with it. Try the spirits by the book.

precepts.text: If sinners entice thee, consent thou not; walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.” The multitude entices: “If they say, Come with us, let us lay wait for blood, let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause: Let us swallow them up alive as the grave; and whole, as those that go down into the pit: We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoil: Cast in thy lot among us; let us all have one purse”.

The answer is the law of Exodus 23: “My son, walk not thou in the way with them; refrain thy foot from their path”. Their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men’s lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil.

precepts.text: They set at nought all his counsel and would none of his reproof; when the fear comes he laughs at the calamity, and they that call then are not answered, for they hated knowledge.
precepts.point: They returned and wept before the Lord, but the Lord would not hearken to their voice nor give ear. When counsel is set at nought until the judgment lands, the weeping comes too late; they that hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord seek him early and do not find him. So they abode in Kadesh many days.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh”. That is Israel here. The Lord had given chance after chance to obey and not fear, and every time the same trial brought the same unbelief. His counsel was set at nought until the judgment fell; only then did they say “We have sinned against the Lord, we will go up and fight”.

Then they set his counsel at nought again. He said “Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest ye be smitten before your enemies”, and they “went presumptuously up into the hill”, boldly doing what they were told not to do, as recorded in Numbers 14. The Amorites came out and chased them as bees do, and destroyed them in Seir unto Hormah: the fear came as desolation, and the destruction as a whirlwind.

“Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. So it was: “ye returned and wept before the Lord; but the Lord would not hearken to your voice, nor give ear unto you.” When counsel is set at nought until the judgment lands, the weeping comes too late. They that hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord seek him early and do not find him, and so they abode in Kadesh many days.

precepts.text: Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you. That is exactly what was read of Samuel: the word of the Lord was not yet revealed to him, and when the Lord called and he turned, the word was made known to him. But because I have called, and ye refused, I also will laugh at your calamity.
precepts.point: What was happening spiritually when the Most High was revealing himself to Samuel and about to pour his word into him? The same thing that happens to all Israel: he stands at the door and knocks. That door is your spirit. The knocking is the Lord calling out through the videos, the flyers, the four chapters a day, the classes; that is the Lord standing and knocking at the spirit of all Israel before he cuts you off.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.” That is exactly what was read of Samuel: the word of the Lord was not yet revealed to him, and when the Lord called and he turned, saying “Speak; for thy servant heareth”, the word was made known to him.

But the other side: “Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded; But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh.”

So warn your brothers and sisters of the nation of Israel: when you hear the Lord calling, through this flyer, these scriptures, this video, turn at his reproof. We do not know when he will cut a man off and leave him to his own devices to destroy himself.

precepts.text: Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: for they hated knowledge, the laws, and would none of my counsel: therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way. Refuse to turn from the drugs, and the drugs destroy you; refuse to stop fornicating, and the sex you love destroys you; refuse to give up the sabbath chasing money, and money destroys you.
precepts.point: What was happening spiritually when the Most High was revealing himself to Samuel and about to pour his word into him? The same thing that happens to all Israel: he stands at the door and knocks. That door is your spirit. The knocking is the Lord calling out through the videos, the flyers, the four chapters a day, the classes; that is the Lord standing and knocking at the spirit of all Israel before he cuts you off.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord.” The knowledge they hated is the laws. “They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof. Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.”

Refuse to turn from the drugs, and the drugs destroy you. Refuse to stop fornicating, and the sex you love destroys you. Refuse to give up the sabbath chasing money, and money destroys you. When he cries, the Lord will not hear.

That is why, when the Lord stands and calls, you answer the first time.

precepts.text: God has poured out his spirit and made his words known, so no one has an excuse; those who refuse will be mocked when their fear comes.
precepts.point: The hidden ones are the key. When you learn your true identity you change your life: less pornography, less marijuana, less going to the doctor, less mass incarceration, no eating pork, no celebrating Christmas or the fourth of July. That repentance is where your power lies, and that is why they work to keep you asleep.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David says if there is iniquity in his hands, let the enemy persecute his soul. Proverbs shows why no one can complain when that judgment comes. “How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge? Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.” God has poured out his spirit and made his words known, so no one has an excuse.

Then the sentence on those who refuse: “Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded; But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh; When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you.”

The hidden ones are the key. When you learn your true identity you change your life: less pornography, less marijuana, less going to the doctor, less mass incarceration, no eating pork, no celebrating Christmas or the fourth of July. That repentance is where your power lies, and that is why they work to keep you asleep. Turn at his reproof now, before the fear comes as desolation.

precepts.text: How long ye simple ones will ye love simplicity, and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge; simple, scorner and fool are synonyms.
precepts.point: Making wise the simple: pay attention to who the simple is, the scorner, the foolish, the youth void of understanding. A lot of times we go out and think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge?” Simple ones loving simplicity, scorners delighting in their scorning, fools hating knowledge: simple, scorner and fool are synonyms.

So the simple that the sure testimony of the Lord makes wise is the scorner and the fool, the one who has been loving simplicity and hating knowledge.

precepts.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
precepts.point: Making wise the simple: pay attention to who the simple is, the scorner, the foolish, the youth void of understanding. A lot of times we go out and think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.” Knowledge begins with the fear of the Lord, and the fool is the one who despises wisdom and instruction.

That fool is the simple and the scorner of Proverbs 1:22, the one the testimony of the Lord makes wise once he stops despising instruction.

precepts.text: For their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood, the same wicked path Solomon says to avoid and turn from.
precepts.point: The path of the just is as the shining light that shineth more and more unto the perfect day, but the way of the wicked is as darkness; they know not at what they stumble.

note.label: Proverbs 4: Wisdom Is the Principal Thing

precepts.why:
“Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil men. Avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, and pass away.” This is the same thing we read in Proverbs 1: “For their feet run to evil, and make haste to shed blood.”

The path of the wicked is the path of feet that run to evil and make haste to shed blood. That is why the warning is so full: avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, pass away. These are the men who sleep not except they have done mischief, who eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.

Their way is darkness and they know not at what they stumble, but the path of the just is the shining light unto the perfect day. Turn from the one and walk in the other.

precepts.text: You have set at nought all counsel and would have none of reproof, matching the man who hated instruction.
precepts.point: Drink waters out of your own cistern and running waters out of your own well. This is a call to stay with your own people and your own nationality.

note.label: Proverbs 5: The Strange Woman and Thy Labours in the House of a Stranger

precepts.why:
The man who despised instruction mourns at the last: “How have I hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof; And have not obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor inclined mine ear to them that instructed me!” The commandments and the prophets are the teachers meant here.

Wisdom said it of him already in Proverbs 1: “But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof”. Setting counsel at nought and refusing reproof is the very thing he confesses too late: he hated instruction and despised reproof.

He ends up almost in all evil in the midst of the congregation and assembly. The one who would have none of reproof is the one who mourns at the last.

precepts.text: Turn you at my reproof, and I will pour out my spirit unto you; the first stipulation is turning at his reproof.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost comes in an order that begins with the law: turn at his reproof and keep the commandments, and then he pours out his spirit and opens the understanding. Only the Most High can give the wisdom to interpret this book, which is the most purchased yet least understood book on the earth.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
The Holy Ghost comes in an order, and it begins with the law. “Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.”

The first stipulation is turning at his reproof. Turn, keep the commandments, and then he pours out his spirit and makes known his words, opening the understanding. The promise of the Father is not given to a man who will not turn.

precepts.text: Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you and make known my words unto you.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is given only to them that obey the Most High; those who will not keep his commandments do not have it, however they claim it.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.”

Christ was exalted to give repentance to Israel, and the spirit is poured out on those who turn at his reproof. Christ came through the loins of David, from Judah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; the law was given to Israel, so repentance from breaking the law is given to Israel. The apostles are his witnesses because their lineage experienced his ministry, death and miracles; popes and denominations are not witnesses. And the Holy Ghost comes to them that turn and obey.

points: The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel. Solomon is giving understanding in this proverb, and from the very top he is basically talking about the fear of the Most High and understanding.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: These verses lay out why the proverbs are given: to know wisdom and instruction, to perceive the words of understanding, to receive the instruction of wisdom, justice, judgment, and equity, to give subtlety to the simple, and to the young man knowledge and discretion.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: A wise man will hear and increase learning, and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels, to understand the proverb and the interpretation, the words of the wise and their dark sayings.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: The fear of the Most High is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction. This is the key that runs through all four chapters.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: My son, hear the instruction of thy father and forsake not the law of thy mother, for they shall be an ornament of grace unto thy head and chains about thy neck.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: A key point is verse 10: my son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not. If somebody who is committing sin entices you or tries to get you to go with them, do not go with them.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: To bring some life to it, look at something like a robbery. If they say come with us, let us lay wait for blood, let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause, that means you are doing evil to the innocent for no reason.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: Let us swallow them up alive as the grave, and we shall find all precious substance and fill our houses with spoil. Whatever you take from this person, you are going to fill your own pockets with their goods.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: Cast in thy lot among us, let us all have one purse. The sinner is enticing you, saying that if you consent, then they will share the spoils of what they get.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: My son, walk not thou in the way with them, refrain thy foot from their path. Solomon is giving wisdom: do not fall into the hands of sinners, do not be enticed by the things they want to do, and do not be enticed by their greediness.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: So are the ways of everyone that is greedy of gain, which taketh away the life of the owners thereof. If you are greedy of gain, you will be going with them, you will be enticed, and you will consent to them.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: Wisdom cries without and utters her voice in the streets, in the chief place of concourse and in the openings of the gates, calling out to the simple ones who love simplicity, the scorners who delight in their scorning, and the fools who hate knowledge.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: Turn ye at my reproof, behold I will pour out my spirit unto you and make known my words unto you. The reproof is the correction of the Most High, that is, His commandments.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: Because I have called and you refused, I have stretched out my hand and no man regarded, but ye have set at nought all my counsel and would none of my reproof, I also will laugh at your calamity and mock when your fear cometh.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me, because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Most High.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: They were none of my counsel and despised all my reproof, all His commandments. Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way and be filled with their own devices. The Most High is going to give you up to whatever you are choosing to do; whatever you put over Him is what He will allow you to do.

note.label: Proverbs 1: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Knowledge

points: For the turning away of the simple shall slay them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them, but whoso hearkeneth unto the Most High shall dwell safely and be quiet from fear of evil.
